sent_to_model:
Hiya, I need help please with a handout for our home birth families. Our team (Riverside community midwives) is redoing the welcome pack and my manager Deb asked me to do the page "Helping your midwife find you" because I am the one who always gets lost lol. It goes in the folder we give at the booking visit and also on our Facebook group for the mums and dads. I want it funny so people actually read it, but the info has to be correct because when it is 3am and baby is coming we really need to get in the house fast. Some of the families are first time, some have done it before, lots of different backgrounds so keep the English simple. Can you write it as a proper document with headings? I wrote down what I could think of on my break, it is below. Please include the calling instructions and a fridge checklist from my notes.

- home birth cover starts from 37 weeks, before that you go to the hospital, we tell everyone at booking but they forget
- two midwives come for the birth, usually separate cars, so two parking spaces if possible
- we carry a lot, gas and air cylinders, the big bag, birthing pool stuff sometimes. arms are tired
- permit zones round Anfield and Kensington, ask the council for visitor permit or leave one on the dashboard ready, we got tickets before
- phone the Riverside birth line when labour starts, not my personal mobile, the line goes to whoever is on call
- once drove round a block of flats in Everton for 20 minutes, flat 14 was not near flat 13, it was other building. dad was waving tea towel from window in the end
- a house with no number only a name 'Rosemary Cottage' in a street of terraces, sat nav took me to a chippy
- staffie called Pippin who loves me too much, jumped on me every visit, I nearly dropped the Entonox
- one family put balloons on the gate like for a party, best idea ever, found it straight away
- walked into wrong house once, door was open, nice old man gave me a Jammie Dodger anyway
- porch light on at night please!! dark streets in winter all look the same
- the what3words thing is good actually, or just send a pin on WhatsApp to the birth line phone
- pets in another room, I love dogs but not during the pushing
- clear the stairs and hallway, no shoes, no washing basket, no Lego
- funny but correct, families should feel welcome not told off
- a little checklist at the end they can tick, maybe to stick on the fridge
- in the Philippines we say the midwife is like family, I want them to feel we are coming as a friend

(About me: community midwife, 50, Liverpool, England. Length: it should come to roughly 800-2,000 words.)

Explains locating and entering the home and carrying equipment, suggesting a what3words location or WhatsApp pin to the birth line phone.
Explains two midwives usually arrive in separate cars; asks for two parking spaces if possible and a council visitor permit obtained or ready where needed.
Asks families to turn on the porch light at night, keep pets in another room, and clear the hallway and stairs.
Uses document headings and ends with a checklist of arrival preparations that families can tick and keep on the fridge.
